Japan Industrial Output Rebounds, Pointing to Economic Resilience
TOKYO--Japan's industrial production recovered in September, showing resilience despite headwinds including higher costs and supply disruptions caused by the war in the Middle East.
Industrial output rose 2.2% from the previous month, compared with August's 2.4% fall, government data showed Friday. That beat the 1.2% rise expected by economists surveyed by Quick.
Japanese businesses were positive on conditions in the fourth quarter, expecting production to rise 5.1% in October and increase 0.8% in November, the data showed.
The recovery in factory activity last month is welcome news for the Bank of Japan, which continues to pursue further interest-rate increases to keep inflation in check.
The central bank is widely expected to keep its policy rate steady at 1.25% later in the day, but many economists and investors anticipate another hike at its next meeting in December.
